gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Carrois Gothic SC feels contemporary and approachable, with curves that stay open at their ends. And Woodgod over it is the loud, vintage half, so the pair's strongest quality is how sharply the two moods split.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-chivo: Chivo sets its lowercase tightly up toward the caps, with visible daylight in every curve. Chivo keeps a long run of text approachable and businesslike, while Woodgod's wide-channeled bowls hold the commanding, vintage note above.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-chocolate-classica: Chocolate Classical Sans reads large and modern, with a broad-nibbed stroke. Woodgod is best at commanding attention with vintage force, while the body font is best at carrying sizable, uncurled lowercase line after line.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-comme: Woodgod's lowercase rises nearly to the capitals, giving it a towering, vintage swagger. Shrink that heading, though, and the commanding feel fades, while Comme stays smooth and modern, its lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-cossette-texte: Cossette Texte reads clean and open, with a prominent x-height and wide-eyed lowercase e. Woodgod's tall, vintage lowercase gives the heading a stitched-thread lightness, while the body's n arches match its stems for a sturdier, steadier feel below.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-duru-sans: Woodgod announces itself with commanding, vintage lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals. And Duru Sans below it reads modern and clean over many lines, its wide-open small letters and dominant bodies hardly bothered by ascenders.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-fresca: Woodgod does best at commanding, vintage display, with tall lowercase and a wide channel into every bowl. But Fresca is better at quiet work, keeping its counters connected to the outside and its crossbars as thick as its stems.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-funnel-sans: Professional in tone, Funnel Sans keeps its stroke widths steady from stem to curve under Woodgod's vintage, commanding heading. And its pried-open e and tiny ascender gaps make a long stretch of text feel clean and unhurried.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-gafata: Woodgod's lowercase climbs almost to the capital height, and its bowls open through wide channels, which gives the heading a vintage, commanding punch. Gafata's strength is restraint.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-geist: Woodgod brings commanding, vintage lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals, each bowl cut with a wide channel. But Geist's every stroke has the same gauge, so its quiet, level words read as solid blocks, and that is the strongest quality here.
